content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Problem:
To calculate the break even point and plot it on a graph, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Identify all fixed costs like rent and insurance (4 hours)
Step 2. Calculate the contribution margin ratio (30 minutes)
Step 3. Determine the break-even point in units (1 hour)
Step 4. Determine the break-even point in total sales dollars (1 hour)
Step 5. Create a data table for the Total Cost line (2 hours)
Step 6. Research variable costs per unit for raw materials (3 days)
Step 7. Validate the accuracy of labor cost estimates (5 hours)
Step 8. Gather historical sales volume data (1 day)
Step 9. Calculate the average variable cost per unit (2 hours)
Step 10. Verify tax implications on net income (4 hours)
Step 11. Draft a preliminary financial summary (3 hours)
Step 12. Review the depreciation schedule for equipment (2 hours)
Step 13. Set the scale for the Y-axis representing dollars (45 minutes)
Step 14. Consult with the marketing department on pricing strategy (2 days)
Step 15. Research current interest rates for business loans (1 hour)
Step 16. Define the range for the X-axis representing units (1 hour)
Step 17. Calculate the total fixed costs sum (30 minutes)
Step 18. Calculate the expected margin of safety (1.5 hours)
Step 19. Confirm the utility cost projections (1 hour)
Step 20. Select the graphing software or tool to use (30 minutes)
Step 21. Perform a sensitivity analysis on price changes (4 hours)
Step 22. Format the final financial report document (2 hours)
Step 23. Plot the break-even point intersection on the chart (15 minutes)
Step 24. Collect all departmental budget requests (1 week)
Step 25. Present the break-even findings to stakeholders (1 hour)
Step 26. Audit the internal procurement logs (1 day)
Step 27. Calculate the slope of the total cost line (40 minutes)
Step 28. Define the unit selling price (20 minutes)
Step 29. List all assumptions made during data collection (2 hours)
Step 30. Archive the raw data files (15 minutes)
Step 31. Calculate the contribution margin per unit (15 minutes)
Step 32. Review the lease agreements for facility costs (3 hours)
Step 33. Interview the production manager regarding waste (4 hours)
Step 34. Run a simulation of best-case sales scenarios (5 hours)
Step 35. Identify the relevant range of production (2 hours)
Step 36. Plot the Total Revenue line on the graph (1 hour)
Step 37. Label the chart title and legend (20 minutes)
Step 38. Conduct a competitive price analysis (1 day)
Step 39. Determine the maximum production capacity (3 hours)
Step 40. Calculate the interest expense on debt (1 hour)
Step 41. Estimate the shipping and handling fees per unit (2 hours)
Step 42. Review the final graph for visual clarity (30 minutes)
Step 43. Calculate the degree of operating leverage (2 hours)
Step 44. Calculate the total variable costs at maximum capacity (1 hour)
Step 45. Document the source of raw material pricing (1 hour)
Step 46. Plot the Total Cost line on the graph (1 hour)
Step 47. Adjust costs for seasonal fluctuations (3 hours)
Step 48. Open a new spreadsheet workbook (5 minutes)
Step 49. Check for any bulk purchase discounts (2 hours)
Step 50. Outline the chart area on the workspace (10 minutes)
Step 51. Draw the Fixed Cost horizontal line (30 minutes)
Step 52. Factor in the monthly maintenance fees (2 hours)
Step 53. Calculate the total costs at various volume levels (2 hours)
Step 54. Compare costs against last year's performance (4 hours)
Step 55. Calculate the weighted average cost of capital (3 hours)
Step 56. Finalize the product unit specifications (1 day)
Step 57. Verify the math on all overhead allocations (4 hours)
Step 58. Calculate the variable cost ratio (30 minutes)
Step 59. Gather the shipping insurance quotes (1 day)
Step 60. Write a summary of the break-even analysis (2 hours)
